concept: A sports business 'follow the money' carousel on the IPL 2027 trade window, two days before retention lists are due. The hero sets two fees against each other: Pant's Rs 27 crore at Lucknow greyed out, his Rs 15 crore at Delhi in bright white, so the pay cut is the story before you read a word. Slide 2 turns the old-fee-to-new-fee gap into gold bars, with Pant's Rs 12 crore cut lit up. Slide 3 flips it with the big exception, Hardik Pandya's raise to Rs 18 crore in the Arshdeep swap. Slide 4 explains what the cuts mean for purses before the Goa auction and asks fans to pick the winning trade. Business gold, type and numbers only: no player photos, no team logos.
caption:
Pant took a Rs 12 crore pay cut to go home.

Lucknow paid a record Rs 27 crore for Rishabh Pant before IPL 2025. He is back at Delhi Capitals for IPL 2027 at a revised Rs 15 crore, with Kuldeep Yadav moving to Lucknow at his existing Rs 13.5 crore.

He is not alone. Liam Livingstone moves from SRH to CSK at Rs 6 crore (down from Rs 13 crore). T Natarajan returns to SRH at Rs 5 crore (down from Rs 10.75 crore).

The big raise: Hardik Pandya joins Punjab Kings at Rs 18 crore, up from Rs 16.35 crore at Mumbai, with Arshdeep Singh going the other way at Rs 18 crore.

Lower fees mean more purse left for the mini-auction in Goa on December 16. Retention lists are reportedly due November 17.
